schemes.description: Warm rain only: cloud water and rain, no ice. For tests, not real forecasts.
schemes.label: Kessler warm rain / MP1

schemes.description: Two-moment scheme with separate graupel and hail, predicting mass and number of each.
schemes.label: Milbrandt-Yau two-moment / MP9

schemes.description: Two-moment ice, snow, rain and graupel, predicting mass and number.
schemes.label: Morrison two-moment / MP10

schemes.description: Two-moment scheme with graupel and hail volume, built for supercells and hail.
schemes.label: NSSL-2 / MP18

schemes.description: No cloud or precipitation physics.
schemes.label: No microphysics

schemes.description: One free ice category whose rime and density evolve, instead of fixed snow, graupel and hail classes.
schemes.label: P3 one-category / MP50

schemes.description: SASE microphysics. Registered as a plan; not in WOOF yet.
schemes.label: SASE microphysics

schemes.description: Thompson with water- and ice-friendly aerosol setting droplet and ice numbers.
schemes.label: Thompson aerosol-aware / MP28

schemes.description: Snow and graupel by mass, rain and cloud ice by mass and number; common for winter precipitation.
schemes.label: Thompson / MP8

schemes.description: WSM6 ice with two-moment warm rain and cloud condensation nuclei.
schemes.label: WDM6 double-moment warm rain / MP16

schemes.description: Single-moment six classes: vapour, cloud, rain, ice, snow, graupel.
schemes.label: WSM6 / MP6

families.what: Clouds and precipitation: how water vapour becomes cloud, rain, snow, graupel and hail.

schemes.description: Scale-aware ensemble convection that tapers itself off as the grid resolves storms.
schemes.label: Grell-Freitas

schemes.description: Deep and shallow convection by mass flux, for grids coarser than about 4 km.
schemes.label: Kain-Fritsch

schemes.description: Mass-flux convection with deep, shallow and mid-level arms.
schemes.label: New Tiedtke

schemes.description: No convection scheme: the grid makes its own storms. The usual choice below about 4 km.
schemes.label: Cumulus off

families.what: Convection too small for the grid to make itself.

schemes.description: Local turbulent-energy boundary layer (Mellor-Yamada-Janjic). Needs the Eta surface layer.
schemes.label: MYJ PBL

schemes.description: Turbulent-energy boundary layer with mass flux, strong in stable nights and shallow cloud.
schemes.label: MYNN PBL

schemes.description: No boundary-layer scheme. Pair with a 3-D turbulence closure below about 1 km.
schemes.label: PBL off

schemes.description: WOOF's own scale-adaptive closure, experimental and not a WRF scheme.
schemes.label: SASE PBL

schemes.description: Scale-aware YSU for grids between about 0.5 and 4 km.
schemes.label: Shin-Hong PBL

schemes.description: Nonlocal boundary layer from Yonsei University; the common default.
schemes.label: YSU PBL

families.what: Mixing of heat, moisture and wind in the lowest one to three kilometres.

schemes.description: Monin-Obukhov surface layer in its original MM5 form.
schemes.label: Classic MM5 surface layer

schemes.description: Eta similarity surface layer, the partner of the MYJ boundary layer.
schemes.label: Eta similarity surface layer

schemes.description: MYNN surface layer, the partner of the MYNN boundary layer.
schemes.label: MYNN surface layer

schemes.description: No surface-layer scheme.
schemes.label: Surface layer off

schemes.description: Monin-Obukhov surface layer with the 2012 revisions.
schemes.label: Revised MM5 surface layer

families.what: Heat, moisture and drag exchanged between the ground and the lowest model level.

schemes.description: Four soil layers with vegetation and snow; the standard land model.
schemes.label: Four-layer Noah LSM

schemes.description: Noah with a canopy layer, layered snow and groundwater options; heavier.
schemes.label: Noah-MP land-surface model

schemes.description: No land model: the ground temperature is held as given.
schemes.label: Land-surface model off

schemes.description: Nine soil levels and layered snow; the land model HRRR uses.
schemes.label: RUC land-surface model

families.what: Soil temperature and moisture, vegetation and snow on the ground.

schemes.description: Clear-sky formulas with no clouds or gases. For tests only.
schemes.label: Analytic clear-sky radiation

schemes.description: Dudhia sunlight only, no infrared. Runs by day only.
schemes.label: Longwave off + WRF Dudhia shortwave

schemes.description: No radiation.
schemes.label: Radiation off

schemes.description: Infrared and sunlight through clouds and gases, both streams (RTE+RRTMGP or the WRF RRTMG port).
schemes.label: RTE+RRTMGP longwave and shortwave

schemes.description: WRF RRTM infrared with Dudhia sunlight; the older pairing.
schemes.label: WRF RRTM longwave + Dudhia shortwave

families.what: Sunlight (shortwave) and infrared (longwave) heating and cooling.

schemes.description: No separate mixing operator: the SASE closure supplies all mixing.
schemes.label: no km_opt operator (closure-supplied mixing)

schemes.description: Fixed mixing coefficients, for tests.
schemes.label: constant K (khdif/kvdif)

schemes.description: Horizontal Smagorinsky mixing; the usual choice with a boundary-layer scheme.
schemes.label: 2-D Smagorinsky

schemes.description: 3-D Smagorinsky mixing for large-eddy runs with the boundary layer off.
schemes.label: 3-D Smagorinsky

schemes.description: 3-D mixing from a predicted turbulent energy, for large-eddy runs with the boundary layer off.
schemes.label: 1.5-order prognostic TKE

families.what: The mixing operator inside the dynamics, apart from the boundary-layer scheme.

presets.why: No cumulus scheme, so the 3 km grid makes its own storms, with Thompson ice and radiation by day and night.
Kain-Fritsch handles the rainbands a 12 km grid cannot resolve, and Morrison carries two-moment ice.
Thompson keeps snow, graupel and rain apart, which the rain, snow and sleet split is read from.
Morrison with Kain-Fritsch on a 12 km grid: 16 times fewer columns than 3 km and a 4 times longer step.

Boundary layer off with a 3-D turbulent-energy closure, because below 1 km the grid resolves the big eddies. 500 m is the finest outer grid Create starts. Daytime only: pick a start and length that stay in daylight.

MYNN mixing with its own cloud fraction, the RUC land surface and Thompson cloud water, with radiation by day and night. Scored against stations and ceilometers on marine fog days, this combination kept the fog and stratus that YSU or Noah each lost part of.
